yearMeaning: The memorial day entered into effect on 1 January 2023 following a 2022 legislative amendment; the first COVID-19 case in Slovakia was confirmed in 2020.
authority: National Council of the Slovak Republic
dateReason: 6 March 2020 was the date of Slovakia's first confirmed COVID-19 case.

sourceEvidence.claim: Current Act 241/1993 section 3(a) lists 6 March as the Day of Victims of the COVID-19 Pandemic.
Legislative text effective 1 January 2023 includes the new memorial day.
The victims' families association Skutočné obete advocated legal recognition of 6 March as a memorial day.
Slovak public broadcaster reported first official commemoration in 2023 and the link to the first confirmed case in 2020.

narratives.en: Slovakia observes the Day of Victims of the COVID-19 Pandemic on 6 March, remembering people who died during the pandemic and the families left behind. The date recalls 6 March 2020, when the country's first COVID-19 case was confirmed. Relatives organized through the association Skutočné obete campaigned for a national day of remembrance. A legislative amendment adopted in 2022 took effect on 1 January 2023, adding the observance to the memorial days in Act 241/1993. The first official annual commemoration followed on 6 March 2023. The date is one of remembrance, not the anniversary of the first recorded death.
narratives.it: La Slovacchia celebra il 6 marzo la Giornata in memoria delle vittime della pandemia di COVID-19, ricordando le persone decedute e i familiari colpiti dal lutto. La data richiama il 6 marzo 2020, quando fu confermato il primo caso di COVID-19 nel Paese. I parenti delle vittime, riuniti nell'associazione Skutočné obete, promossero il riconoscimento di una giornata nazionale della memoria. Una modifica legislativa approvata nel 2022 entrò in vigore il 1° gennaio 2023, inserendo la ricorrenza nella legge 241/1993. La prima commemorazione annuale ufficiale si tenne il 6 marzo 2023. La data non corrisponde al primo decesso registrato.
narratives.es: Eslovaquia conmemora el 6 de marzo el Día de las Víctimas de la Pandemia de COVID-19, en recuerdo de las personas fallecidas y de sus familias. La fecha remite al 6 de marzo de 2020, cuando se confirmó el primer caso de COVID-19 en el país. Los familiares de las víctimas, agrupados en la asociación Skutočné obete, impulsaron la creación de una jornada nacional de recuerdo. Una reforma legislativa aprobada en 2022 entró en vigor el 1 de enero de 2023 e incorporó la fecha a la Ley 241/1993. La primera conmemoración anual oficial tuvo lugar el 6 de marzo de 2023. La fecha no señala la primera muerte registrada.
narratives.fr: La Slovaquie commémore le 6 mars la Journée des victimes de la pandémie de COVID-19, en mémoire des personnes décédées et de leurs proches. Cette date rappelle le 6 mars 2020, jour de la confirmation du premier cas de COVID-19 dans le pays. Des familles de victimes réunies au sein de l'association Skutočné obete ont demandé la création d'une journée nationale de mémoire. Une modification législative adoptée en 2022 est entrée en vigueur le 1er janvier 2023 et a inscrit cette journée dans la loi 241/1993. La première commémoration annuelle officielle a eu lieu le 6 mars 2023. Cette date ne correspond pas au premier décès recensé.
narratives.de: Die Slowakei begeht am 6. März den Gedenktag für die Opfer der COVID-19-Pandemie. Er erinnert an die Verstorbenen und ihre Angehörigen. Das Datum verweist auf den 6. März 2020, als der erste COVID-19-Fall des Landes bestätigt wurde. Hinterbliebene, die sich im Verein Skutočné obete zusammengeschlossen hatten, setzten sich für einen nationalen Gedenktag ein. Eine 2022 verabschiedete Gesetzesänderung trat am 1. Januar 2023 in Kraft und nahm den Tag in Gesetz 241/1993 auf. Die erste offizielle jährliche Gedenkveranstaltung fand am 6. März 2023 statt. Das Datum bezeichnet nicht den ersten registrierten Todesfall.
narratives.pt: A Eslováquia assinala em 6 de março o Dia em Memória das Vítimas da Pandemia de COVID-19, recordando as pessoas falecidas e as suas famílias. A data remete para 6 de março de 2020, quando foi confirmado o primeiro caso de COVID-19 no país. Familiares das vítimas, reunidos na associação Skutočné obete, defenderam a criação de um dia nacional de memória. Uma alteração legislativa aprovada em 2022 entrou em vigor em 1 de janeiro de 2023 e incluiu a data na Lei 241/1993. A primeira comemoração anual oficial ocorreu em 6 de março de 2023. A data não assinala a primeira morte registada.
